change: Advance the existing four-stage town lighting by Japan local time while preserving explicit development stage overrides.
canonicalSources: adopted lighting behavior from Staging PR #947
expectedChanges: Default the existing town lighting to the four established periods according to Asia/Tokyo local time: morning 05:00, noon 08:00, evening 17:00, night 20:00.
Re-evaluate at the next minute and on tab visibility restoration, without adding a frame loop or persisting user data.
Preserve explicit lighting=morning|noon|evening|night|off query overrides; lighting=auto requests clock-driven behavior.
Add boundary tests for all four intervals, midnight, unsupported time zone fallback and explicit override behavior.
ownerDecisions: The author now requests automatic town lighting. Japan Standard Time is used because Yumaniwa is a Japanese town.
hqDecisions: Use the Asia/Tokyo IANA time zone rather than the visitor device time zone. Keep the selected default schedule at 05:00 morning, 08:00 noon, 17:00 evening and 20:00 night. Keep query overrides for development comparison.
rulesApplied: Lock scope before implementation. Trusted base Scope/Risk/Impact and static gates. No drawing loop or storage changes.
rollback: Revert this isolated Staging PR to restore the fixed noon default.
outOfScope: automatic change to the approved appearance of any period
permanent user interface or saved preferences

problem: Lighting remains fixed at noon unless a development query manually selects another stage.
currentContract: Shared town lighting supports morning, noon, evening, night, and off. It defaults to noon and allows a stage query parameter.
whyExistingIsInsufficient: There is no wall-clock stage mapping or automatic refresh.
design: Resolve the current Asia/Tokyo hour and minute when loaded, schedule a single timer for the next minute, and refresh when visibility returns. Keep manual query overrides fixed.

migration: No persisted data or URL migration.
compatibility: Existing query controls and complete lighting off state remain available.
